To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the biographical interview can be used to explore the identity formation process of the repeat offender in prison.

(1) Schütze’s biography work method has the potential to be used as a rehabilitation tool for prisoners, (2) the triple bind of narration inherent in the method makes this possible, (3) the method can be used with a range of different types of interviewees, and (4) it can be used to explore a wide range of different social problems.

(a) the interviewees were not repeat offenders, they were repeat victims of their social environment; (b) their life stories were shaped by their parents and by the state; (c) their life stories are characterized by a lack of agency, a lack of control over their lives, and a lack of self-esteem and self-worth; and, (d) their life stories can be used to develop rehabilitation programmes that are more effective than current practice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how to understand the process of identity construction in a social science research setting and the potential for such an approach to have rehabilitation value.
the question of how to make social research more meaningful and more useful for the individual, and in this sense we are in line with the aims of Fritz Schütze himself.
how social science can make a difference to people’s lives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Schütze's method offers a unique way of understanding the process of identity and identity formation, which can be used in prison sociology to help the prisoner in their rehabilitation.
this article offers a new approach to the study of identity formation, a new approach to prison research and a new approach to rehabilitation.
the Schütze method of biography is a valuable tool in social science research and prison research in particular.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are in favour of the use of Schütze’s interview technique as an instrument to study identity formation in prison research, as well as in other areas of social science enquiry.
we have found Schütze’s methodology to be a useful tool for understanding the identity formation of repeat offenders in prison.

the ‘triple binding of narration’ is an effective tool for the researcher to gain a better understanding of the interviewee’s social world, and to help the interviewee to understand their own life and identity in a new and more critical way.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the biographical interview is a powerful tool for the researcher to understand the individual’s social position and for the individual to understand their own position.
the biographical interview can be used to understand the identity formation process and the social construction of self in the life story of the individual.
the biographical interview method is not just for biographical research.
